<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:nu}
Let $G$ be semiregular. Then $\nu_2(G)=\iota(G)v/2$, and
$\nu_t(G)\le v^{t-1}$, for $t\ge 3$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
A $2$-subset $\{x,y\}$ fails to be free if and only if some $g\in G\setminus\{1\}$
interchanges $x$ and $y$. Such an element is an involution. Each involution
$g$ yields the $v/2$ pairs $\{x,gx\}$. Different involutions yield different
pairs, because at most one element of $G$ maps $x$ to $gx$. Hence
$\nu_2(G)=\iota(G)v/2$.

Let $t\ge 3$, and let $T$ be a $t$-subset of $V$ with $gT=T$, for some
$g\in G\setminus\{1\}$. Then $T$ is a union of cycles of $g$, and each cycle has length
$\operatorname{ord}(g)\ge 2$. Hence $T$ is determined by $g$ and by one point from each
of these cycles. There are at most $m\le v$ elements $g$ and at most
$\lfloor t/2\rfloor$ cycles. Therefore
$\nu_t(G)\le v^{1+\lfloor t/2\rfloor}\le v^{t-1}$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:pairs}
Let $k\ge t\ge 1$ be integers and let $G\le\mathrm{Sym}(V)$. Then
\[
 P_G(v,k,t)\ \le\ \Bigl(\binom{v}{t}-\nu_t(G)\Bigr)\Big/\binom{k}{t}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:general}
Let $k>t\ge 2$ be integers and let $\varepsilon>0$. There exists a number
$\delta=\delta(k,t,\varepsilon)>0$ with the following property. Let $V$ be a
set of $v\ge k$ points, and let $G\le\mathrm{Sym}(V)$ be a permutation group with
$\beta_{k,t}(G)\le\delta$. Then
\[
 P_G(v,k,t)\ \ge\ \bigl(1-\varepsilon-\alpha_{k,t}(G)\bigr)
 \binom{v}{t}\Big/\binom{k}{t}.
\]
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:geh}
Let $k>t\ge 2$ be integers and let $\varepsilon>0$. There exist an integer
$v_0=v_0(k,t,\varepsilon)$ and a number $c=c(k,t)>0$ with the following
property. Let $G$ be a semiregular permutation group on a set of $v\ge v_0$
points. Then
\[
 P_G(v,k,t)\ \ge\ \Bigl((1-\varepsilon)\binom{v}{t}-c\,\nu_t(G)\Bigr)
 \Big/\binom{k}{t}.
\]
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{ex:elementary}
Let $G=\mathbb{Z}_2^{a}$ act on itself by translation, so that $v=2^{a}$. Every
$2$-subset $\{x,y\}$ of $G$ is mapped to itself by the translation by $x+y$.
Hence $\nu_2(G)=\binom{v}{2}$, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:pairs} gives $P_G(v,k,2)=0$, for all $k\ge 2$. Let $k\ge 3$ be odd, and
let $B$ be a block of a $G$-invariant $2$-$(v,k,1)$ packing. The stabiliser of $B$ is a $2$-group. The order of the stabiliser divides $k$, because $B$ is a union of orbits of its stabiliser on $V$, and each of these orbits has as many points as the stabiliser has elements. Hence the stabiliser of $B$ is trivial. Thus the packing is free, and it is
empty by Proposition~\ref{prop:pairs}. Therefore every
$G$-invariant $2$-$(v,k,1)$ packing is empty, whereas $2$-$(v,k,1)$ packings
with $(1-o(1))\binom{v}{2}/\binom{k}{2}$ blocks exist.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:kahn}
For every integer $s\ge 2$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$
with the following property. Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a hypergraph in which every edge
has at most $s$ vertices, every vertex has degree at most $D$, and every two
distinct vertices have codegree at most $\delta D$. Then the edges of $\mathcal{H}$
can be partitioned into at most $(1+\varepsilon)D$ matchings. In particular,
$\mathcal{H}$ has a matching with at least $|E(\mathcal{H})|/((1+\varepsilon)D)$ edges.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:sep-basic}
Let $B$ be a $t$-separated $k$-subset of $V$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item The set $B$ is free, and every $t$-subset of $B$ is free.
\item Distinct $t$-subsets of $B$ lie in distinct $G$-orbits.
\item If $T$ is a $t$-subset of $B$ and $T\subseteq gB$, for some $g\in G$,
then $g=1$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Let $g\in G\setminus\{1\}$, and let $T$ be a $t$-subset of $B$. Since $B$
is $t$-separated, $|B\cap gB|\le t-1$.

(i) If $gB=B$, then $|B\cap gB|=k\ge t$. If $gT=T$, then
$T\subseteq B\cap gB$, and so $|B\cap gB|\ge t$. Both conclusions contradict $|B\cap gB|\le t-1$. Hence
$B$ and $T$ are free.

(ii) If $gT\subseteq B$, then $gT\subseteq B\cap gB$, and so
$|B\cap gB|\ge t$. This is impossible. Hence no $t$-subset of $B$ other than
$T$ lies in the orbit of $T$.

(iii) If $T\subseteq gB$, then $T\subseteq B\cap gB$, and so
$|B\cap gB|\ge t$. This is impossible. Hence $T\subseteq hB$ with $h\in G$
only if $h=1$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:sep-count}
Let $k\ge t\ge 2$ be integers. A $k$-subset $B$ of $V$ is $t$-separated if
and only if $N(B)=0$. The number of $k$-subsets of $V$ that fail to be
$t$-separated is at most $\alpha_{k,t}(G)\binom{v}{k}$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Both statements were shown in Section~\ref{sec:main}. We have $N(B)=0$ if
and only if $B$ satisfies \eqref{eq:sep}, and Markov's inequality gives
$N(B)=0$, for all but at most $\alpha_{k,t}(G)\binom{v}{k}$ of the
$k$-subsets $B$ of $V$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
Let $k>t\ge 2$. The \emph{orbit hypergraph} $\mathcal{H}_k$ has vertex set $X$ and one edge for each orbit $[B]$ of $t$-separated $k$-subsets of $V$, and
this edge is the set
\[
 \partial[B]=\{[T] : T\subseteq B,\ |T|=t\}.
\]
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:matching-packing}
Let $k>t\ge 2$, and let $\mathcal{M}$ be a matching in $\mathcal{H}_k$. Then the union $\mathcal{B}$
of the orbits that correspond to the edges of $\mathcal{M}$ is a free $G$-invariant
$t$-$(v,k,1)$ packing with $m|\mathcal{M}|$ blocks.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
The family $\mathcal{B}$ is $G$-invariant, and its blocks are free by
Lemma~\ref{lem:sep-basic}. Let $B_1$ and $B_2$ be distinct blocks that both
include a $t$-subset $T$. If $B_2=gB_1$, for some $g\in G$, then $g\ne 1$ and
$T\subseteq B_1\cap gB_1$, which contradicts the separation of $B_1$.
Otherwise $\partial[B_1]$ and $\partial[B_2]$ are distinct edges of $\mathcal{M}$
and both contain $[T]$, which contradicts disjointness.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:restricted}
Let $k>t\ge 2$ be integers, let $\varepsilon>0$, and let $\delta$ be the
number given by Theorem~\ref{thm:kahn} for $s=\binom{k}{t}$ and
$\varepsilon$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a set of $t$-separated $k$-subsets of $V$ such
that $gB\in\mathcal{F}$, for all $B\in\mathcal{F}$ and all $g\in G$. Let $D>0$ be a number
with the following two properties. Every $t$-subset of $V$ is included in at
most $D$ members of $\mathcal{F}$. For all $t$-subsets $T$ and $S$ of $V$ in distinct
orbits, at most $\delta D$ members of $\mathcal{F}$ include $T$ and an image of $S$.
Then
\[
 P_G(\mathcal{F},t)\ \ge\ \frac{|\mathcal{F}|}{(1+\varepsilon)D}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be the hypergraph that consists of the vertices of $\mathcal{H}_k$ and of
the edges $\partial[B]$ with $B\in\mathcal{F}$. The members of $\mathcal{F}$ are free by
Lemma~\ref{lem:sep-basic}, so their orbits have size $m$, and $\mathcal{H}$ has
$|\mathcal{F}|/m$ edges.

Let $T$ be a free $t$-subset of $V$. Every edge of $\mathcal{H}$ that contains $[T]$
has the form $\partial[B]$ with $B\in\mathcal{F}$ and $T\subseteq B$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:sep-basic}(iii), the orbit $[B]$ contains exactly one set that
includes $T$. Hence the degree of $[T]$ in $\mathcal{H}$ is the number of members of
$\mathcal{F}$ that include $T$, which is at most $D$.

Let $[T]$ and $[S]$ be distinct vertices. Every edge that contains both has
the form $\partial[B]$ with $B\in\mathcal{F}$ and $T\subseteq B$, and $B$ includes an
image of $S$. Hence the codegree of $[T]$ and $[S]$ is at most $\delta D$.

By Theorem~\ref{thm:kahn}, the hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ has a matching $\mathcal{M}$ with at
least $|\mathcal{F}|/((1+\varepsilon)mD)$ edges. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:matching-packing}, the union of the orbits that correspond to
the edges of $\mathcal{M}$ is a free $G$-invariant $t$-$(v,k,1)$ packing with $m|\mathcal{M}|$ blocks. The blocks of this packing belong to $\mathcal{F}$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:semireg}
Let $k>t\ge 2$ be integers and let $G$ be semiregular. There is a constant
$c_1=c_1(k,t)\ge 1$ such that
\[
 \alpha_{k,t}(G)\le c_1\Bigl(\frac{1}{v}+\nu_t(G)\Big/\binom{v}{t}\Bigr)
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 \beta_{k,t}(G)\le\frac{c_1}{v}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Let $J\subseteq V$ with $|J|=j$. If $j\le k$, then
$\Pr[J\subseteq\mathbf{B}]=\binom{v-j}{k-j}/\binom{v}{k}$, and otherwise this
probability is zero. In both cases
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prob}
 \Pr[J\subseteq\mathbf{B}]\ \le\ \Bigl(\frac{k}{v}\Bigr)^{j}.
\end{equation}
If $J$ includes a $t$-subset $T$, then likewise
\begin{equation}\label{eq:condprob}
 \Pr[J\subseteq\mathbf{B}\mid T\subseteq\mathbf{B}]\ \le\ \Bigl(\frac{k}{v}\Bigr)^{j-t},
\end{equation}
because this probability is $\binom{v-j}{k-j}/\binom{v-t}{k-t}$ if $j\le k$,
and zero otherwise.

A $t$-subset $T'$ lies in $B\cap gB$ if and only if $T=g^{-1}T'$ satisfies
$T\subseteq B$ and $gT\subseteq B$. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:alpha-sum}
 \alpha_{k,t}(G)=\sum_{g\in G\setminus\{1\}}\ \sum_{T}
 \Pr[T\cup gT\subseteq\mathbf{B}],
\end{equation}
where $T$ ranges over the $t$-subsets of $V$. Let $T$ be a $t$-subset of $V$
and let $g\in G\setminus\{1\}$. Let $\Gamma_g(T)$ be the directed graph on
$T$ with an arc from $x$ to $gx$ whenever $x\in T$ and $gx\in T$. The number
of arcs is $i=|T\cap gT|$, and $|T\cup gT|=2t-i$. Every vertex has at most
one outgoing arc and at most one incoming arc, and there are no loops. Hence
every component of $\Gamma_g(T)$ with at least one arc is a directed path or
a directed cycle. A directed cycle is a cycle of the permutation $g$, so it
has exactly $\operatorname{ord}(g)$ vertices and $\operatorname{ord}(g)$ arcs. Let $p$ be the number of
components that are paths with at least one arc, and let $q$ be the number of
components that are cycles. A path with $j$ arcs has $j+1$ vertices, and a
cycle with $j$ arcs has $j$ vertices. Therefore the components with at least
one arc have $i+p$ vertices in total.

We bound the contribution to \eqref{eq:alpha-sum} of the pairs $(T,g)$ for
which $\Gamma_g(T)$ has a given isomorphism type. The number of types depends
only on $t$. Consider one type and one element $g$. The type determines the number of vertices of each component. A component
that is a directed path is determined by $g$ and by its initial vertex. A
component that is a directed cycle is determined by $g$ and by any one of
its vertices. Hence there are at most $v^{p+q}$ choices for the vertices of
the components with at least one arc, and
at most $v^{t-i-p}$ choices for the remaining points of $T$. Thus at most
$v^{t-i+q}$ sets $T$ arise. By \eqref{eq:prob}, each contributes at most
$(k/v)^{2t-i}$. The contribution of this type and this $g$ is therefore at
most $k^{2t}v^{q-t}$.

If $q=0$, then summation over the at most $v$ elements $g$ gives at most
$k^{2t}v^{1-t}\le k^{2t}v^{-1}$. Suppose that $q\ge 1$. Each cycle has at
least two arcs, so $q\le\lfloor t/2\rfloor$. If $t\ge 3$, then
$\lfloor t/2\rfloor\le t-2$, and summation over $g$ gives at most
$k^{2t}v^{1+q-t}\le k^{2t}v^{-1}$. If $t=2$, then $q=1$, the two arcs form a
cycle of length two, and $g$ is an involution. Summation over the involutions
gives at most $k^{2t}\iota(G)\,v^{-1}$. Since
$\nu_2(G)=\iota(G)v/2$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:nu}, we have $\iota(G)/v\le\nu_2(G)/\binom{v}{2}$. The bound on $\alpha_{k,t}(G)$
follows, with $c_1$ at least $k^{2t}$ times the number of types.

Let $T$ and $S$ be $t$-subsets of $V$. Then
\[
 \mathbb{E}\bigl[M_{T,S}(\mathbf{B})\,\big|\,T\subseteq\mathbf{B}\bigr]
 =\sum_{\substack{g\in G\\ gS\ne T}}\Pr[T\cup gS\subseteq\mathbf{B}\mid T\subseteq\mathbf{B}].
\]
Let $g\in G$ with $gS\ne T$. Then $|T\cup gS|\ge t+1$. If
$gS\cap T\ne\emptyset$, then $gy=x$, for some $y\in S$ and $x\in T$.
Semiregularity gives at most $t^2$ such elements $g$, and each contributes at
most $k/v$ by \eqref{eq:condprob}. If $gS\cap T=\emptyset$, then
$|T\cup gS|=2t$, and $g$ contributes at most $(k/v)^{t}$. There are at most
$m\le v$ such elements, and $v(k/v)^{t}\le k^{t}/v$. Hence
$\beta_{k,t}(G)\le(t^2k+k^{t})/v$.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- restated-1: body_md -->
{Proposition}{prop:pairs}
Let $k\ge t\ge 1$ be integers and let $G\le\mathrm{Sym}(V)$. Then
\[
 P_G(v,k,t)\ \le\ \Bigl(\binom{v}{t}-\nu_t(G)\Bigr)\Big/\binom{k}{t}.
\]
<!-- end restated-1 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a free $G$-invariant $t$-$(v,k,1)$ packing. Let $T$ be a
$t$-subset of $V$ that is not free, and let $g\in G\setminus\{1\}$ with
$gT=T$. Suppose that a block $B$ includes $T$. Then $gB$ includes $gT=T$.
Since $B$ is free, $gB\ne B$, and so two distinct blocks include $T$. This is
impossible. Hence no block includes a $t$-subset that is not free. The blocks
of $\mathcal{B}$ therefore include at most $\binom{v}{t}-\nu_t(G)$ of the
$t$-subsets of $V$, and each $t$-subset lies in at most one block.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- restated-2: body_md -->
{Theorem}{thm:general}[$G$-invariant Erd\H{o}s--Hanani theorem]
Let $k>t\ge 2$ be integers and let $\varepsilon>0$. There exists a number
$\delta=\delta(k,t,\varepsilon)>0$ with the following property. Let $V$ be a
set of $v\ge k$ points, and let $G\le\mathrm{Sym}(V)$ be a permutation group with
$\beta_{k,t}(G)\le\delta$. Then
\[
 P_G(v,k,t)\ \ge\ \bigl(1-\varepsilon-\alpha_{k,t}(G)\bigr)
 \binom{v}{t}\Big/\binom{k}{t}.
\]
<!-- end restated-2 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Put $D=\binom{v-t}{k-t}$. Let $\delta$ be the number given by
Theorem~\ref{thm:kahn} for $s=\binom{k}{t}$ and $\varepsilon$, and suppose
that $\beta_{k,t}(G)\le\delta$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the set of all $t$-separated
$k$-subsets of $V$. As shown before the definition of $\mathcal{H}_k$, we have
$gB\in\mathcal{F}$, for all $B\in\mathcal{F}$ and all $g\in G$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:sep-count}, $|\mathcal{F}|\ge(1-\alpha_{k,t}(G))\binom{v}{k}$. Every
$t$-subset of $V$ is included in at most $D$ members of $\mathcal{F}$. By
\eqref{eq:codeg}, for all $t$-subsets $T$ and $S$ in distinct orbits, at most
$\beta_{k,t}(G)D\le\delta D$ members of $\mathcal{F}$ include $T$ and an image of
$S$. Since $\binom{v}{k}/D=\binom{v}{t}/\binom{k}{t}$,
Proposition~\ref{prop:restricted} gives
\[
 P_G(v,k,t)\ \ge\ P_G(\mathcal{F},t)\ \ge\ \frac{1-\alpha_{k,t}(G)}{1+\varepsilon}
 \binom{v}{t}\Big/\binom{k}{t}.
\]
The theorem follows, because $(1-x)/(1+\varepsilon)\ge 1-\varepsilon-x$ for
all $x\ge 0$.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- restated-3: body_md -->
{Theorem}{thm:geh}[Semiregular groups]
Let $k>t\ge 2$ be integers and let $\varepsilon>0$. There exist an integer
$v_0=v_0(k,t,\varepsilon)$ and a number $c=c(k,t)>0$ with the following
property. Let $G$ be a semiregular permutation group on a set of $v\ge v_0$
points. Then
\[
 P_G(v,k,t)\ \ge\ \Bigl((1-\varepsilon)\binom{v}{t}-c\,\nu_t(G)\Bigr)
 \Big/\binom{k}{t}.
\]
<!-- end restated-3 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Let $\delta=\delta(k,t,\varepsilon/2)$ be the number given by
Theorem~\ref{thm:general}, and let $c_1=c_1(k,t)$ be the constant of
Lemma~\ref{lem:semireg}. By Lemma~\ref{lem:semireg}, $\beta_{k,t}(G)\le c_1/v$ and
$\alpha_{k,t}(G)\le c_1/v+c_1\nu_t(G)/\binom{v}{t}$. Let
$v\ge\max\{k,c_1/\delta,2c_1/\varepsilon\}$. Then
$\beta_{k,t}(G)\le\delta$ and $c_1/v\le\varepsilon/2$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:general} gives
\[
 P_G(v,k,t)\ \ge\ \Bigl(1-\varepsilon
 -c_1\,\nu_t(G)\Big/\binom{v}{t}\Bigr)\binom{v}{t}\Big/\binom{k}{t}.
\]
This is the assertion with $c=c_1$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:few}
Let $k>t\ge 2$ be integers and let $\varepsilon>0$. There exists an integer
$v_1=v_1(k,t,\varepsilon)$ such that
\[
 (1-\varepsilon)\binom{v}{t}\Big/\binom{k}{t}\ \le\ P_G(v,k,t)\ \le\
 \binom{v}{t}\Big/\binom{k}{t},
\]
for every semiregular permutation group $G$ with at most three involutions on
a set of $v\ge v_1$ points.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
The upper bound is \eqref{eq:trivial}. By Lemma~\ref{lem:nu},
$\nu_2(G)=\iota(G)v/2\le 3v/2$, and $\nu_t(G)\le v^{t-1}$, for $t\ge 3$. Hence
$\nu_t(G)\le 2v^{t-1}$. Let $c$ and $v_0$ be the numbers given by
Theorem~\ref{thm:geh} for $\varepsilon/2$. For $v\ge v_0$, Theorem~\ref{thm:geh} gives
$P_G(v,k,t)\ge\bigl((1-\varepsilon/2)\binom{v}{t}-2cv^{t-1}\bigr)/\binom{k}{t}$.
Since $\binom{v}{t}\ge(v/t)^t$, we have
$2cv^{t-1}\le(\varepsilon/2)\binom{v}{t}$, for all
$v\ge 4ct^{t}/\varepsilon$.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:ooc-packing}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a family of $w$-subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_v$, and put
$\mathcal{B}=\{C+a : C\in\mathcal{C},\ a\in\mathbb{Z}_v\}$. Then $\mathcal{C}$ is a $(v,w,\lambda)$ OOC if
and only if $\mathcal{B}$ is a free $G$-invariant $(\lambda+1)$-$(v,w,1)$ packing
with $v|\mathcal{C}|$ blocks. Moreover, every free $G$-invariant
$(\lambda+1)$-$(v,w,1)$ packing on $\mathbb{Z}_v$ has this form, where $\mathcal{C}$ is an
arbitrary set of representatives of the orbits of $G$ on its blocks.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
The family $\mathcal{B}$ is $G$-invariant. Suppose that $\mathcal{C}$ is a $(v,w,\lambda)$
OOC. Let $C,C'\in\mathcal{C}$ and $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}_v$ with $(C,a)\ne(C',b)$. Then
$|(C+a)\cap(C'+b)|=|C\cap(C'+b-a)|\le\lambda$. This follows from the autocorrelation property if $C=C'$, because then
$b-a\ne 0$, and from the cross-correlation property if $C\ne C'$. Since $\lambda<w$, we have $C+a\ne C'+b$. Hence $\mathcal{B}$ has
$v|\mathcal{C}|$ blocks, every block is free, and every two distinct blocks have at
most $\lambda$ common points. Thus $\mathcal{B}$ is a free $G$-invariant
$(\lambda+1)$-$(v,w,1)$ packing.

Suppose now that $\mathcal{B}$ is a free $G$-invariant $(\lambda+1)$-$(v,w,1)$
packing with $v|\mathcal{C}|$ blocks. Then the sets $C+a$ with $C\in\mathcal{C}$ and
$a\in\mathbb{Z}_v$ are pairwise distinct. Two distinct blocks of a
$(\lambda+1)$-$(v,w,1)$ packing have at most $\lambda$ common points. Hence
$|C\cap(C+a)|\le\lambda$, for all $C\in\mathcal{C}$ and $a\ne 0$, and
$|C\cap(C'+a)|\le\lambda$, for all distinct $C,C'\in\mathcal{C}$ and all $a$. Thus
$\mathcal{C}$ is a $(v,w,\lambda)$ OOC.

Finally, let $\mathcal{B}'$ be a free $G$-invariant $(\lambda+1)$-$(v,w,1)$ packing
on $\mathbb{Z}_v$, and let $\mathcal{C}$ be a set of representatives of the orbits of $G$ on
$\mathcal{B}'$. Every orbit has $v$ blocks. Hence
$\mathcal{B}'=\{C+a : C\in\mathcal{C},\ a\in\mathbb{Z}_v\}$, and $\mathcal{B}'$ has $v|\mathcal{C}|$ blocks.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:ooc}
Let $G=\mathbb{Z}_v$ act on $\mathbb{Z}_v$ by translation. Then
\[
 \Phi(v,w,\lambda)=\frac{1}{v}\,P_G(v,w,\lambda+1).
\]
Consequently, for all integers $\lambda\ge 1$ and $w\ge\lambda+2$,
\[
 \Phi(v,w,\lambda)=(1-o(1))\,
 \frac{(v-1)(v-2)\cdots(v-\lambda)}{w(w-1)\cdots(w-\lambda)}
 \qquad (v\to\infty).
\]
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
The identity $\Phi(v,w,\lambda)=P_G(v,w,\lambda+1)/v$ is
Lemma~\ref{lem:ooc-packing}. The group $G$ is cyclic, so it has at most one
involution. The asymptotic formula follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:few} with $t=\lambda+1$ and $k=w$, because
$\binom{v}{\lambda+1}/(v\binom{w}{\lambda+1})$ is the right-hand side of
\eqref{eq:ooc-upper}.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:nd}
Let $G=\mathbb{Z}_T$ act on $V$ by translation of the last coordinate. The largest
size of a $(\Lambda_1\times\dots\times\Lambda_{d-1}\times T,w,\lambda)$ OOC
is
\[
 \frac{1}{T}\,P_G(\Lambda T,w,\lambda+1).
\]
Consequently, for all integers $\lambda\ge 1$ and $w\ge\lambda+2$, this
largest size is
\[
 (1-o(1))\,\frac{\Lambda\,(\Lambda T-1)(\Lambda T-2)\cdots(\Lambda T-\lambda)}
 {w(w-1)\cdots(w-\lambda)}
 \qquad(\Lambda T\to\infty).
\]
The estimate is uniform in $d$ and in $\Lambda_1,\dots,\Lambda_{d-1},T$.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:ooc-packing} applies with $\mathbb{Z}_T$ in place of
$\mathbb{Z}_v$ and $V$ in place of $\mathbb{Z}_v$. This proof shows that a family $\mathcal{C}$ of $w$-subsets of $V$ is a $(\Lambda_1\times\dots\times\Lambda_{d-1}\times T,w,\lambda)$ OOC if and only
if the sets $C+a$, with $C\in\mathcal{C}$ and $a\in\mathbb{Z}_T$, form a free $G$-invariant
$(\lambda+1)$-$(\Lambda T,w,1)$ packing with $T|\mathcal{C}|$ blocks. It also shows
that every free $G$-invariant $(\lambda+1)$-$(\Lambda T,w,1)$ packing
consists of the sets $C+a$, with $C\in\mathcal{C}$ and $a\in\mathbb{Z}_T$, for a family
$\mathcal{C}$ of $w$-subsets of $V$. Hence the largest size of a code is
$P_G(\Lambda T,w,\lambda+1)/T$. The group $G$ is cyclic, and the asymptotic
formula follows from Corollary~\ref{cor:few} with $v=\Lambda T$, $t=\lambda+1$ and
$k=w$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:oospc}
Let $G=\mathbb{Z}_m\times\mathbb{Z}_n$ act on itself by translation. Then
\[
 \Psi(m,n,w,\lambda)=\frac{1}{mn}\,P_G(mn,w,\lambda+1).
\]
Consequently, for all integers $\lambda\ge 1$ and $w\ge\lambda+2$,
\[
 \Psi(m,n,w,\lambda)=(1-o(1))\,
 \frac{(mn-1)(mn-2)\cdots(mn-\lambda)}{w(w-1)\cdots(w-\lambda)}
 \qquad(mn\to\infty).
\]
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:ooc-packing} applies with $\mathbb{Z}_m\times\mathbb{Z}_n$ in
place of $\mathbb{Z}_v$, and gives the identity
$\Psi(m,n,w,\lambda)=P_G(mn,w,\lambda+1)/(mn)$. The group $G$ acts regularly
and has at most three involutions. The asymptotic formula follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:few} with $v=mn$, $t=\lambda+1$ and $k=w$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:cyclic}
Let $w$ and $\delta$ be integers with $2\le\delta\le w-1$, let $\ell$ be a
divisor of $n$, and let $G$ be the group generated by the cyclic shift of
$\mathbb{Z}_n$ by $\ell$ positions. The maximum number of codewords in a binary
quasi-cyclic code of index $\ell$, length $n$, constant weight $w$ and
minimum distance at least $2\delta$, in which every codeword has $n/\ell$
distinct images under $G$, is
\[
 P_G(n,w,w-\delta+1).
\]
Consequently, this maximum is
\[
 (1-o(1))\binom{n}{w-\delta+1}\Big/\binom{w}{w-\delta+1}
 =(1-o(1))\,A(n,2\delta,w)
 \qquad(n\to\infty),
\]
uniformly over all divisors $\ell$ of $n$.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Put $t=w-\delta+1$. A binary quasi-cyclic code of index $\ell$, length $n$,
constant weight $w$ and minimum distance at least $2\delta$, in which every
codeword has $n/\ell$ distinct images under $G$, is a $G$-invariant
$t$-$(n,w,1)$ packing in which every block has trivial stabiliser. Hence it
is a free $G$-invariant $t$-$(n,w,1)$ packing, and every free $G$-invariant
$t$-$(n,w,1)$ packing is a code with these properties. Therefore the maximum
number of codewords is $P_G(n,w,t)$. The group $G$ is cyclic, and
$w>t\ge 2$. The asymptotic formula follows from Corollary~\ref{cor:few} with $v=n$ and $k=w$, and from
R\"odl's theorem for $A(n,2\delta,w)$.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:gd}
Let $k>t\ge 2$ be integers. Then
\[
 P_G(\mathcal{F}_k,t)=(1-o(1))\binom{\Lambda}{t}T^{t}\Big/\binom{k}{t}
 \qquad(\Lambda T\to\infty),
\]
uniformly over all $\Lambda\ge k$ and all $T\ge 1$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
The upper bound is \eqref{eq:gd-bound}. For the lower bound, we apply Proposition~\ref{prop:restricted} to $\mathcal{F}=\mathcal{F}_k$. We
have $|\mathcal{F}|=\binom{\Lambda}{k}T^{k}$, and $B+a\in\mathcal{F}$, for all
$B\in\mathcal{F}$ and all $a\in\mathbb{Z}_T$. Every $B\in\mathcal{F}$ satisfies
$B\cap(B+a)=\emptyset$, for all $a\in\mathbb{Z}_T\setminus\{0\}$, so it is
$t$-separated. A transversal of size $j\le k$ is included in exactly
$\binom{\Lambda-j}{k-j}T^{k-j}$ members of $\mathcal{F}$, and a subset of $V$ that is
not a transversal is included in none. Put
\[
 D=\binom{\Lambda-t}{k-t}T^{k-t}.
\]
Then every $t$-subset of $V$ is included in at most $D$ members of $\mathcal{F}$. For
$t\le j<k$, the ratio of $\binom{\Lambda-j-1}{k-j-1}T^{k-j-1}$ to
$\binom{\Lambda-j}{k-j}T^{k-j}$ is $(k-j)/((\Lambda-j)T)$. Since
$\Lambda\ge k$, this ratio is at most $\rho=(k-t)/((\Lambda-t)T)$, and
$\rho\le k/v$. Hence a subset of $V$ of size $j\ge t$ is included in at most
$\rho^{j-t}D$ members of $\mathcal{F}$.

Let $T_0$ and $S$ be $t$-subsets of $V$ in distinct orbits of $\mathbb{Z}_T$. At most
$t^2$ elements $a\in\mathbb{Z}_T$ satisfy $(S+a)\cap T_0\ne\emptyset$. For each of
them $|T_0\cup(S+a)|\ge t+1$, and at most $\rho D$ members of $\mathcal{F}$ include
$T_0\cup(S+a)$. At most $T$ elements $a$ satisfy
$(S+a)\cap T_0=\emptyset$. For each of them $|T_0\cup(S+a)|=2t$, and at most
$\rho^{t}D$ members of $\mathcal{F}$ include $T_0\cup(S+a)$. Now
$T\rho^{t}\le k^{t}/(\Lambda^{t}T^{t-1})\le k^{t}/v$, because $t\ge 2$.
Hence at most $(t^{2}k+k^{t})D/v$ members of $\mathcal{F}$ include $T_0$ and an image
of $S$.

Let $\varepsilon>0$, and let $\delta$ be the number given by
Theorem~\ref{thm:kahn} for $s=\binom{k}{t}$ and $\varepsilon$. Let
$v\ge(t^{2}k+k^{t})/\delta$. Proposition~\ref{prop:restricted} gives
\[
 P_G(\mathcal{F}_k,t)\ \ge\ \frac{\binom{\Lambda}{k}T^{k}}{(1+\varepsilon)D}
 =\frac{1}{1+\varepsilon}\binom{\Lambda}{t}T^{t}\Big/\binom{k}{t}.
\]
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:amopp}
We have
\[
 \Phi^{*}(\Lambda\times T,w,\lambda)=\frac{1}{T}\,P_G(\mathcal{F}_w,\lambda+1).
\]
Consequently, for all integers $\lambda\ge 1$ and $w\ge\lambda+2$,
\[
 \Phi^{*}(\Lambda\times T,w,\lambda)=(1-o(1))\,
 \binom{\Lambda}{\lambda+1}T^{\lambda}\Big/\binom{w}{\lambda+1}
 \qquad(\Lambda T\to\infty),
\]
uniformly over all $\Lambda\ge w$ and all $T\ge 1$.
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:ooc-packing} applies with $\mathbb{Z}_T$ in place of
$\mathbb{Z}_v$ and $V$ in place of $\mathbb{Z}_v$. This proof shows that a family $\mathcal{C}$ of transversal $w$-subsets of $V$ is a code with at most one pulse per
wavelength if and only if the sets $C+a$, with $C\in\mathcal{C}$ and $a\in\mathbb{Z}_T$,
form a $G$-invariant group divisible $(\lambda+1)$-packing with block size
$w$ and with $T|\mathcal{C}|$ blocks. It also shows that every $G$-invariant group
divisible $(\lambda+1)$-packing with block size $w$ consists of the sets
$C+a$, with $C\in\mathcal{C}$ and $a\in\mathbb{Z}_T$, for a family $\mathcal{C}$ of transversal
$w$-subsets of $V$. This proves the identity
$\Phi^{*}(\Lambda\times T,w,\lambda)=P_G(\mathcal{F}_w,\lambda+1)/T$. The asymptotic
formula follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:gd} with
$t=\lambda+1$ and $k=w$.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
